decisions.decision: The rollback plan relies on operators retaining an upgraded copy for re-upgrade because 1.4.0 can read the live file but drops due times when it saves.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected to run 1.4.0 normally and then re-upgrade its live file while retaining both the original due times and any ticket changes made during rollback.
decisions.where: record/03-research.md:15, summary on 1.4.0 writes and re-upgrade recovery

decisions.decision: With DUE_TIMES=on, the service refuses to start if an existing data file contains tickets without due times.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the service to start and keep serving legacy responses while reporting that activation is blocked.

decisions.decision: The work stops at a local handoff and leaves the production migration and activation to operations.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected the delivery to include coordinating and carrying out the production rollout.

decisions.decision: Tickets created while DUE_TIMES is off have their due times fixed at creation using the hours in effect then.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected tickets created before activation to be stamped during backfill using the hours chosen for launch.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:6, R-1 Immutable due times; record/03-research.md:15, summary

decisions.decision: When overdue=true is combined with both status and priority, an overdue ticket is included if it matches either of those two filters.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected a ticket to match both status and priority as well as being overdue, as the existing API guide describes for the two ordinary filters.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9, R-2 Gated exposure and overdue retrieval; repo/docs/api.md:76–77, List tickets

decisions.decision: The service reads response-time overrides at startup, so applying new hours to future tickets requires restarting it.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted operators to update the hours for future tickets while the service is running.

decisions.decision: Operators can rerun backfill on a partially stamped file and the command fills only the missing due times.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected a one-time migration that rejects a partially stamped file and requires operators to resolve it before retrying.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:12, R-3 Backfill and rollback; record/03-research.md:15, summary

decisions.decision: The overdue filter is applied before pagination, so page sizes and continuation cursors are based on the matching tickets.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected overdue filtering within each ordinary ticket page, keeping the ordinary cursor boundaries even when a page has few or no matches.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9, R-2 Gated exposure and overdue retrieval; record/02-discovery.md:15, Q10

decisions.decision: When due times are enabled, any value of the overdue query parameter other than the exact string true is silently ignored.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected overdue=false to select non-overdue tickets and malformed values to return a 400 error.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:9, R-2 Gated exposure and overdue retrieval

decisions.decision: The raw CLI output keeps its existing columns and the weekly report keeps its existing output, even when due times are enabled.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted a trailing due column in the raw CLI output so scripts could read it without moving any existing columns.

decisions.decision: Enabling due times adds them to the human-readable CLI as well as to HTTP ticket responses.
decisions.alternative: They might have meant for due times to appear only in HTTP responses and for the operator CLI to keep its current output.

decisions.decision: The spec keeps the existing audit behavior and exposes due through ticket views.
decisions.alternative: They might have wanted the audit history to record when a due time was first assigned, including during backfill.

decisions.decision: The due value is stored as an ISO timestamp, consistent with the API’s UTC timestamp convention.
decisions.alternative: They might have expected due to use a numeric Unix timestamp for their integrations.
